questions.text:
Refer to Text A, "One way and another", on page 2 of the resource booklet.

Discuss how the writer explores the ways people respond to the details of life, referring to at least TWO specific aspects of written texts.
questions.markingGuide:
ACHIEVEMENT (3-4 marks): Develop a relevant critical discussion in response to the question, showing engagement with the text. Make and evaluate a range of relevant points showing understanding of how at least TWO aspects of the text have been crafted to create meaning. Include specific and relevant details from the text to support the discussion.

MERIT (5-6 marks): Develop a convincing critical discussion showing informed engagement with the text. Make and evaluate relevant points showing convincing understanding of how at least TWO aspects have been crafted to create meaning. Begin to weave specific details from the text into the response to effectively support the discussion. Potentially link points to matters beyond the text.

EXCELLENCE (7-8 marks): Develop a sophisticated or original critical discussion showing insightful engagement with the text. Make and evaluate relevant points showing perceptive understanding of how at least TWO aspects have been crafted to create meaning. Weave specific and judiciously chosen details into the response to effectively support and expand the discussion. Trace the development of ideas throughout the text and link points to other contexts such as human experience, society, and the wider world.

Relevant aspects might include: audiences and purposes; ideas (e.g. nature provides surprising beauty, memories bring joy, the connected nature of things, having things both ways); language features (e.g. simile, emotive language, personal pronouns, rhetorical question); structures (e.g. stanza use, time/chronology/memory, outside-inside-outside, duality).

questions.text:
Refer to BOTH Text A and Text B.

Compare how the writers reflect on people's experiences of change, referring to at least TWO specific aspects of written texts. You may refer to one or both texts in your response.
questions.markingGuide:
ACHIEVEMENT (3-4 marks): Develop a relevant critical discussion in response to the question, showing engagement with the text(s). Make and evaluate a range of relevant points showing understanding of how at least TWO aspects of the text(s) have been crafted to create meaning. Include specific and relevant details from the text(s) to support the discussion.

MERIT (5-6 marks): Develop a convincing critical discussion showing informed engagement with the text(s). Make and evaluate relevant points showing convincing understanding of how at least TWO aspects have been crafted to create meaning. Begin to weave specific details from the text(s) into the response to effectively support the discussion. Potentially link points to matters beyond the text(s).

EXCELLENCE (7-8 marks): Develop a sophisticated or original critical discussion showing insightful engagement with the text(s). Make and evaluate relevant points showing perceptive understanding of how at least TWO aspects have been crafted to create meaning. Weave specific and judiciously chosen details into the response to effectively support and expand the discussion. Trace the development of ideas throughout the text(s) and link points to other contexts such as human experience, society, and the wider world.

Relevant aspects might include: audiences and purposes; ideas (e.g. changes that are expected or not anticipated, changes that are welcome or that bring challenges, material changes or changes to ideas, changes to plumbing and changes to society); language features (e.g. personal pronouns - in the poem 'I' is the writer who reflects on the change also experienced by 'we', presumably the people in the family/street; in the prose 'I' is a woman expected to change and 'he' is a man challenged by change; emotive language - in the poem change is appreciated as ambivalence 'swanky'/'extravagance', in the prose change is appreciated through 'nightmare' as negative); structures (e.g. use of time to show how change can be slower than expected in terms of names, or faster than realised in terms of plumbing).
